name: poly-lsp
description: Unified lint/format via the poly daemon: format-on-save, lint-on-save diagnostics, batch commands.

commands.title: Poly: Create go.work for the Open Go Modules

poly.serverPath.description: Path to the poly binary. Relative paths resolve against the first workspace folder; empty uses the bundled binary, then `poly` from PATH.

poly.lintOnSave.description: Publish lint diagnostics when a supported file is opened or saved.

poly.format.enabled.description: Let poly rewrite files: Format Document, format-on-save, Format Selection, and the trailing-whitespace and final-newline fixes .editorconfig asks for on save. Turning it off suspends all of them at once -- the point being to stop formatting for a while without disabling the extension or hunting through per-language settings. Linting is unaffected: not wanting a file rewritten is not the same as not wanting to know what is wrong with it. There is a status bar switch for this next to the Poly item, and `Poly: Toggle Formatting` in the command palette.

poly.deadCodeCodeLens.enabled.description: Show an `analyze dead code` link on the first line of code in every file poly can answer about: Go (golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode), TypeScript and JavaScript (knip), Python (vulture). Clicking it runs `poly deadcode` in a terminal over that file's whole project — the go.work build list, the npm project, the Python project. Nothing runs until it is clicked: whole-program reachability costs a build, so it is asked rather than watched.

poly.languageServers.description: Run the language server a project's own toolchain provides and route hover, go-to-definition, declaration, type definition, implementation, references, outline, completion, signature help, symbol highlight, folding, expand selection, rename and code actions to it. Nine are known: gopls (Go), rust-analyzer (Rust), clangd (C/C++), sourcekit-lsp (Swift), terraform-ls (Terraform), lua-language-server (Lua), bash-language-server (Shell), buf (Protobuf), arity (R). Code actions arrive as lightbulb actions only — the `source.*` kinds `editor.codeActionsOnSave` runs are left out, because VSCode runs those before the formatter and they would rewrite the same lines poly is about to format. Poly's own lint findings stay: the server's diagnostics are merged with them rather than replacing them, so selene and swiftlint keep reporting. Off by default: it overlaps with the official extension for that language, so remove that extension before turning this on. Poly never installs these servers — they come from PATH, and which features work is whatever the server itself declares.

poly.languageServerLogs.description: Forward a downstream language server's own stderr to the Poly output channel. On by default. clangd and terraform-ls write a line per request; gopls, rust-analyzer, sourcekit-lsp and lua-language-server are quiet unless something is wrong. Turning this off discards that output entirely rather than asking each server to be quieter — not all of them can be. Poly's own reports, including a server that is missing or failed to start, are unaffected.

poly.updateCheck.enabled.description: Periodically check GitHub Releases for new Poly versions (also covers poly-syntax-highlight).

poly.updateCheck.intervalDays.description: Days between automatic update checks; 0 checks on every startup.
